recent_posts.title: Building a self-hosted coding agent with Gemma 4 26B on a single GPU
recent_posts.summary: A hands-on walkthrough of building a self-hosted coding agent using Google's Gemma 4 26B model quantized to 4-bit (Q4_K_M), running on a single NVIDIA A10G GPU via Snowflake's Snowpark Container Services. The architecture uses three Docker containers: llama.cpp for inference with an OpenAI-compatible API, a FastAPI sandbox for code execution, and a React frontend. Key gotchas covered include Snowflake stage volume limitations, HuggingFace's Xet storage migration causing silent download hangs, GPU driver availability during Docker builds, and ARM vs x86 image issues. The honest cost analysis concludes self-hosting makes most sense when GPU hardware is already paid for, while acknowledging that Claude and GPT-4o still outperform open-weight models on complex reasoning.

recent_posts.title: Building an AI complaint triage app with Snowflake Cortex in one session
recent_posts.summary: A Snowflake Solutions Engineer built a working AI-assisted complaint triage prototype for a state regulatory agency in a single session using Snowflake Cortex Code (CoCo). The app uses a Cortex Agent with four tools, three RAG indexes (Cortex Search over statutes, case precedents, and document checklists), and Cortex Analyst for plain-English analytics. The frontend is React + Vite + Tailwind with an Express.js backend, deployed on Snowpark Container Services with Snowflake's built-in OAuth for auth. The post covers synthetic data generation, the three-stage human-in-the-loop workflow (intake, investigator review, legal review), and the argument that AI coding assistants make custom internal tools economically viable for small user bases that previously couldn't justify the build cost.

recent_posts.title: dbt for Cortex AI: Harvesting patterns as Snowflake Cortex Code Skills
recent_posts.summary: A Snowflake engineer introduces 'dbt-cortex-pipeline', a Cortex Code skill that automates building unified dbt projects with integrated Cortex AI services (Semantic View, Cortex Search, Cortex Agent) on Snowflake. The skill supports three scenarios: net-new project creation, extending existing dbt projects with AI services, and migrating Dynamic Table pipelines to dbt. It promises 2x-3x acceleration over manual setup. The post also shares best practices for building custom Cortex Code skills, including modularization, lean markdown files, proper trigger words, negative guardrails, and iterative evaluation with eval datasets.

recent_posts.title: Migrating Your Shopify Data Pipeline from REST to GraphQL with Openflow and Snowflake
recent_posts.summary: Shopify deprecated its admin REST API in favor of GraphQL, requiring data pipeline migrations. This walkthrough covers rebuilding a Shopify-to-Snowflake pipeline using Openflow (Apache NiFi) and Shopify's GraphQL Bulk Operations API. Instead of paginating through thousands of REST requests, the new approach submits a bulk export job, polls for completion, downloads the resulting JSONL file, and loads it into a Snowflake internal stage. Key design patterns include using flow files as state machines to track job progress, Parameter Contexts for environment-agnostic configuration, and Controller Services for reusable Snowflake connections. The post also covers Snowflake network rules and external access integrations for both Shopify and Google Cloud Storage, and notes limitations like asynchronous processing, rate limits, and fixed JSONL output format.

recent_posts.title: The Snowflake OAuth Role That Existed — But Didn’t
recent_posts.summary: A production debugging story about a subtle Snowflake OAuth failure affecting SCIM-provisioned users. When rolling out a Snowflake-managed MCP Server with per-user OAuth authentication, roughly a third of users received a misleading 'role does not exist or not authorized' error despite the role being fully granted. After three hours of investigation, the root cause was an undocumented Snowflake OAuth validation: the target session role's ownership chain must trace back through the standard RBAC hierarchy (SECURITYADMIN/SYSADMIN/USERADMIN). Roles created by Okta's SCIM provisioner are owned by OKTA_PROVISIONER, which sits outside this hierarchy, causing OAuth to silently reject them while Snowsight and other connectors continued working fine. The fix is transferring role ownership to SECURITYADMIN using COPY CURRENT GRANTS, then re-granting the role to the SCIM provisioner WITH GRANT OPTION so provisioning continues uninterrupted.

recent_posts.title: Snowflake Cortex AI — Complete Developer Guide 2026
recent_posts.summary: Snowflake Cortex AI is a fully managed, serverless suite of AI and ML services that runs directly within the Snowflake Data Cloud, eliminating the need to move data outside secure environments. The guide covers the full Cortex AI suite including: AI SQL functions (AI_COMPLETE, AI_SENTIMENT, AI_EMBED, AI_REDACT, AI_TRANSCRIBE, and more), Cortex Search for hybrid keyword and semantic search on unstructured data, Cortex Analyst for natural language to SQL conversion, Document AI for extracting structured data from documents, Cortex Guard for responsible AI safety filtering, Cortex Code (Coco) as a data-engineering-focused AI coding agent, and Cortex Agents with Snowflake Intelligence UI. The author shares practical experience building RAG pipelines, document assistant bots, and analytics tools, noting both strengths and limitations observed in real-world use.

recent_posts.title: Becoming an AI Data Architect with SnowPro Advanced Architect
recent_posts.summary: A practical guide to passing the SnowPro Advanced Architect certification exam, emphasizing architectural thinking over feature memorization. Covers a 5-step preparation strategy including scheduling the exam early, following the official study guide, building deep domain knowledge across Architecture, Security, Data Engineering, and Performance, and practicing scenario-based questions. Key exam tips include identifying hidden constraints in questions, preferring cost-efficient and native Snowflake solutions, and understanding when NOT to use specific features like Snowpipe or data sharing.

recent_posts.title: From All-or-Nothing to Graceful Degradation: DML Error Logging in Snowflake
recent_posts.summary: Snowflake's DML Error Logging feature (ERROR_LOGGING = TRUE) enables graceful degradation for INSERT, UPDATE, and MERGE operations. Instead of rolling back an entire batch when a single row fails, Snowflake inserts valid rows normally and routes failed rows to an auto-created error table with full metadata including error code, message, source column, and original row data. The post covers enabling/disabling the feature, querying the ERROR_TABLE() function, error recovery patterns, change tracking via streams on views, access control with GRANT SELECT ERROR TABLE, session-level opt-out, Snowpipe Streaming integration, performance considerations, and key limitations such as lack of support for COPY INTO and multi-table inserts.

recent_posts.title: How to configure scheduled automatic backups in Snowflake
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to configuring scheduled automatic backups in Snowflake, covering backup policy creation with cron and interval schedules, attaching policies to backup sets, verifying backups, and managing policies (suspend, resume, swap). Also explains the two cost components: serverless compute credits for execution and standard storage charges for retained data. Aimed at teams needing retention beyond Snowflake's 90-day time travel window for compliance or cybersecurity requirements.

recent_posts.title: Snowflake AI SQL User Guide: AI_SIMILARITY
recent_posts.summary: AI_SIMILARITY is a Snowflake Cortex AI SQL function that returns a float between 0 and 1 representing semantic similarity between two text strings. Unlike traditional string comparison functions like EDITDISTANCE or JAROWINKLER_SIMILARITY, it understands meaning rather than just characters. The guide walks through 7 practical use cases with full SQL examples: basic string comparison, boundary value testing, semantic search with ranking, threshold-based filtering, cross-row self-join comparisons, fuzzy deduplication of company names, and zero-shot category prediction using CASE/GREATEST. The function works as a scalar that drops into SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, or CASE clauses. Advanced tips include combining it with AI_EMBED to pre-compute embeddings and AI_FILTER for two-pass pipelines.

top_posts.title: SKILLs MD for Analytics: How We Made Snowflake Intelligence Agents Reliable for Production
top_posts.summary: PDQ solved AI agent hallucinations in production analytics by encoding Standard Operating Procedures as SKILLs—version-controlled, agent-executable contracts that define inputs, logic, validation, and guardrails. Instead of scaling multiple specialized agents with long prompts, they built one agent with a library of SKILLs deployed via Git-Ops to Snowflake Dynamic Tables and indexed through Cortex Search. This approach eliminated inconsistent answers, improved quality through mandatory validation steps, and made agent reasoning auditable like code. The architecture separates SKILL discovery (lightweight semantic search) from execution (loading complete SOPs) to preserve context windows while ensuring deterministic analytical workflows.

top_posts.title: Why Apache Iceberg Is Not “Just Another Table Format”
top_posts.summary: Apache Iceberg is a table format specification that sits between file formats (Parquet, ORC) and compute engines, solving critical failures of the Hive era: slow query planning via directory listing, silent schema corruption from position-based column tracking, and lack of safe concurrent writes. Iceberg replaces directory-based tracking with a versioned metadata tree, enabling file-level statistics for query pruning, ACID transactions via immutable snapshots with atomic commits, and metadata-only schema evolution using permanent column IDs. Unlike a traditional warehouse, Iceberg delivers warehouse-grade guarantees on open, decoupled object storage — but shifts operational responsibility (compaction, snapshot expiration) to the user. Major adoption signals include Snowflake achieving full parity with native tables, AWS S3 Tables with built-in Iceberg support, and companies like LinkedIn and Airbnb reporting significant performance and cost gains.

top_posts.title: Eliminating Redundancies in ETL With Iceberg Tables on Snowflake
top_posts.summary: Zello streamlined its ETL pipeline by employing Apache Iceberg tables, Snowflake externally managed Iceberg tables, and dbt transformations. This change eliminated redundant data storage steps, leading to significant cost savings and a more flexible and scalable data architecture. The new approach ensures a single source of truth, reducing storage costs and simplifying the ETL process. Key aspects include better schema management, optimized querying, and seamless integration with multiple data engines.

top_posts.title: Using Kumo in Snowflake for Smarter Product Recommendation
top_posts.summary: Kumo, a powerful ML platform, integrates with Snowflake to enhance product recommendations by leveraging Graph Neural Networks (GNNs). This integration simplifies the development of predictive models without needing extensive data preparation or intricate coding. Kumo enables easier prediction of customer purchases, driving sales and improving recommendation strategies. The post provides a step-by-step guide to setting up data, registering schemas, building predictive models, evaluating performance, and productionizing the models within Snowflake.
